text.p: The European Union's rice management committee on Thursday held a preliminary discussion before postponing consideration of detailed rules on compensatory aid for rice producers, an EU official said on Friday.

Under the reform of the rice regime there is to be a gradual reduction in the intervention price for rice. EU producers will get area compensatory payments similar to those which apply in the cereals sector.
"Further talks will be held" the official said.
The first area payments are due to be issued for the 1997/98 marketing year next year.
The committee also postponed discussion on amending the draft regulation on aid for the supply of rice to the so called Poseidom country's.
The draft regulation (980/92) covering supplies to Guyana, Martinique and Guadeloupe has been delayed because the committee was waiting for France to supply figures.
The committee postponed a decision on a special measure export tender for 100,000 tonnes of Greek maize.
Talks on import quotas for Thai and other country manioc quotas as well as quotas for potatoes and for manioc starch were also postponed.
